response:
Here is my review of [2026-10-28-leo-chief-of-staff-plan.md](file:///home/sheep/agent-shared/knowledge/plans/2026-10-28-leo-chief-of-staff-plan.md) and [leo-persona-study.md](file:///home/sheep/projects/leo-research/leo-persona-study.md) against the codebase and prior plans. No files were edited.

---

### (1) What I disagree with or would cut

1. **Cut the `tasks` table and chore sync (Phase 1) — it conflicts with [2026-10-25-calendar-plan.md](file:///home/sheep/agent-shared/knowledge/plans/2026-10-25-calendar-plan.md#L57-L63) and forces KB proposal spam.**
   In the calendar plan (agreed 3 days ago), chores from `maintenance.md` and `cleaning.md` go to Google Tasks (`chore_log` in SQLite; `maintenance.md` "Last performed" stays human-curated; `due = max(chore_log, md)`). Your Phase 1 builds a competing SQLite task manager and says: *"Done maintenance/cleaning items: Leo files the 'last done' update as a KB change proposal."* Look at [cleaning.md](file:///srv/household/life/household/cleaning.md): there are 10 weekly chores (`CW01`–`CW10`) and 6 monthly ones. Filing a git diff via [`kb_changes.propose()`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/shared/kb_changes.py#L70-L110) every time Sheep vacuums or takes out the trash means Sheep taps `[Done]` in the meeting and immediately gets hit with a second Telegram `<pre>` diff message asking him to tap `[Apply]` to commit a date change to `/srv/household/life`. Furthermore, [`kb_changes.decide()`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/shared/kb_changes.py#L167-L169) checks blob SHA hashes (`_blob(life, f) != h`): if Leo files two maintenance proposals in one debrief touching `cleaning.md`, applying the first changes the blob hash and marks the second proposal `stale`!
   *Fix:* Drop the `tasks` table and KB diff proposals for routine chores. Record completions in a `chore_log` table (as designed in the calendar plan) or keep ad-hoc action items as rows in `event_checks` (`kind='agent'`) / a simple `todo` list without auto-proposing git commits to `maintenance.md`/`cleaning.md`.

2. **Cut multi-turn meeting state (`meetings` table, open/close lifecycle, 45-min idle timer, AI-written minutes).**
   A modal state machine in [`telegram_bot.py`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/agents/telegram_bot.py) ("while open, Sheep's plain text goes to Leo... closes on 'thanks Leo' / `[Done]` / 45 min idle, and Leo then writes the minutes") is premature abstraction and creates fragile UX traps:
   - [`poll_forever()`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/agents/telegram_bot.py#L1074-L1103) blocks on `getUpdates(timeout=50)`. To close a meeting on a 45-minute idle timeout and write minutes, the poll loop now has to run background timers and fire an unprompted Sonnet call when Sheep walks away.
   - What happens if Sheep is mid-meeting and sends a photo of a recipe or a serial label, or replies to a recipe card, or Moose messages her chat?
   - Every turn in an open meeting that re-runs [`agent.run_agent()`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/shared/agent.py#L174-L223) with the full pack, tool loop, `verify.check`, and revision loop will cost ~$0.08–$0.15 *per message*, not per meeting. A 5-turn meeting is $0.50–$0.75 ($30–$45/month for two a day, blowing past the $30 cap).
   *Fix:* Make Leo **stateless per turn**, extending [`recent_exchanges()`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/agents/telegram_bot.py#L179-L190) (which already threads the last N turns within 30–45 minutes from `agent_runs`). Saying "Leo" (or `/leo`, or tapping the nudge) delivers the pre-built pack + initial check-in buttons in one shot. Follow-up replies naturally thread via `recent_exchanges` with the pack injected into the prompt if a pack was opened today. Decisions are recorded inline via the `remember` tool during the turn—no separate "close meeting and write minutes" LLM call needed.

3. **Cut `agent/leo.md` as a parallel prompt system; put Leo in [`agent/playbook.md`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/agent/playbook.md).**
   [`shared/playbook.py`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/shared/playbook.py#L33-L42) loads `General` + `<Task Section>` + active learned rules from `agent_proposals`, and [`reflection_agent.py`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/agents/reflection_agent.py#L243) inspects `playbook.md` to propose rules. If Leo's instructions live in `agent/leo.md`, either Leo ignores learned rules from `agent_proposals` or we have two prompt loaders. Put the Leo persona in `playbook.md` (in `General` for Sheep's runs, plus a `Briefing` / `Debrief` section).

4. **Cut LLM-scored mood words and mid-meeting message redaction.**
   Having local Gemma score free-text mood words into 1–5 integers and intercepting mid-meeting sentences to replace them with `"Sheep added a note about how he feels (kept local)"` is over-engineered and jarring:
   - If Sheep is talking to Leo and says *"I'm worn out today, let's skip the yard work"*, and the privacy router swallows his message so Leo only sees *"Sheep added a note about how he feels (kept local)"*, Leo doesn't know Sheep asked to skip yard work!
   *Fix:* Two inline button rows (`Energy: 1 2 3 4 5`, `Mood: 1 2 3 4 5`) on the pack/check-in card give exact 1–5 scores with zero model calls. If Sheep wants to add a private journal note, make it an explicit reply to the check-in prompt (or `/note`), stored raw in `checkins.words` and never sent to cloud. Don't hijack normal conversation turns with a "feelings" interceptor.

5. **Fold the Dev Board into a deterministic `/dev` command or tool, not a daily briefing staple.**
   Scanning `knowledge/plans/`, git branches across `~/projects/scratch-*`, `staging..master` rev-lists, and Claude memory files twice a day mixes developer meta-work into life management. Keep it on-demand (`/leo board` or a `dev_board` tool Leo only calls when asked about system work).

---

### (2) Risks you missed

6. **Critical state bug when Sheep never says "Leo" (Heartbeat cursor advancement & double-nudge).**
   Look at [`heartbeat_agent.py`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/agents/heartbeat_agent.py#L194-L201): `gate()` computes `new_state` (`bill_rowid`, `sync_id`, `goals`, `feeds`), runs due `event_checks` (`kind='agent'`), and reads `agent_outbox`. Currently, it **only** saves `new_state`, marks `event_checks` `done`, and sets `agent_outbox.flushed_at` *after* `telegram.send()` succeeds.
   - If the 07:30 timer builds the pack and saves `new_state` at 07:30, and Sheep never says "Leo" that day (and ignores the 10:00 nudge), then bill emails, goal transitions, due follow-ups, and held outbox messages are **silently lost forever** unless the 10:00 fallback sends the full pack.
   - Conversely, your plan says: *"the 10:00 nudge is one message: 'Morning, sir. Three items, one needs you today.' with a [Start] button. If Leo fails (model down, error), the heartbeat's old digest text goes out instead at 10:00."* If Leo is **up** at 10:00, it sends the 1-line nudge, not the pack—so if Sheep is busy all day and never taps `[Start]`, he never sees today's bill statements, feed failures, or held messages!
   - Also: if nothing changed in `gate()`, no follow-ups are due, and `agent_outbox` is empty ("Nothing → silent"), does 10:00 or 21:00 still nudge Sheep? Nudging twice a day when nothing needs him violates the `Quiet` goal in [`goals.md`](file:///srv/household/life/goals/goals.md#L60) and the Calendar plan's `"Nothing → silent" stays` principle.
   *Fix:* Do not advance `agent_state['heartbeat']`, mark follow-ups `done`, or flush `agent_outbox` until the pack text is actually delivered to Telegram. And at 10:00, if there are pending items and Sheep hasn't opened the briefing, **send the deterministic pack itself** (with the check-in / action buttons attached) rather than a teaser nudge that hides the information behind another tap. If the pack has 0 items, send no nudge at all.

7. **Interaction with the 4/day message budget and the Nov 2 retirements.**
   - Look at [`shared/telegram.py`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/shared/telegram.py#L26-L29): `UNBUDGETED = {"telegram_bot", "feedback_ack", "heartbeat_agent"}`. Today is **Oct 28**; `financial_agent` (00:00) and `synthesis_agent` (Mon 00:00) are still running until at least Nov 2. `financial_agent` is **budgeted** (1/day), `event_check_agent` is budgeted, `bills_agent` monthly/non-critical is budgeted, and on Sunday/Monday `health_agent` (2 messages: Sheep + Moose), `synthesis_agent`, and `review_agent` all fire (`NEVER_HELD`, so they increment `sent_today()`!).
   - If Leo's 10:00 and 21:00 nudges are **budgeted** (2/day), then between 00:00 `financial_agent` (1) + 10:00 nudge (2) + any `event_check` or `calendar` evening check (3) + 21:00 nudge (4), the 4/day budget is exhausted every single day, and on Sunday/Monday (when `health_agent` + `synthesis_agent` + `review_agent` use 4 slots by 07:45), the 10:00 and 21:00 nudges will be **held in `agent_outbox`** by `telegram.send()`! A nudge held in `agent_outbox` until tomorrow's digest is useless.
   - Furthermore, the Calendar plan ([`2026-10-25-calendar-plan.md`](file:///home/sheep/agent-shared/knowledge/plans/2026-10-25-calendar-plan.md#L9)) explicitly states: *"No proactive calendar message ships until the nightly financial_agent / health_agent sends stop."* Putting Calendar Step 2's Today block and evening prep into Phase 0 before Nov 2 violates that prerequisite unless the morning pack is strictly the existing `heartbeat_agent` slot.
   - Note also: [`telegram.send_one()`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/shared/telegram.py#L107-L128) currently hardcodes `budgeted=False` when calling `record()`, and does **not** check `sent_today() >= budget()`. Since a nudge with a `[Start]` button must use `send_one(..., reply_markup=...)`, it wouldn't even count as budgeted in current code unless `send_one` is changed.

8. **Privacy of `checkins` and Moose's chat isolation.**
   - Adding `checkins` to `LOCAL_TABLES` in [`shared/agent_tools.py`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/shared/agent_tools.py#L22) blocks `query_db` and `db_schema`, which is right. Verify that `/srv/household/seed-agent.db` (the nightly rebuild script for Moose's seed DB in [2026-10-26-moose-account-plan.md](file:///home/sheep/agent-shared/knowledge/plans/2026-10-26-moose-account-plan.md#L29)) also strips `checkins` and `meetings`, just as it strips `cal_events` and `agent_messages`.
   - In [`telegram_bot.py`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/agents/telegram_bot.py#L193-L218), `converse(text, who=who)` serves **both** Sheep and Moose (`who="moose"`). Your Phase 2 says: *"plain-text chat outside meetings goes to Leo (replaces the conversation agent)"*. Moose must **not** get Leo calling her "sir", referencing Sheep's `mood_signal()`, or exposing Sheep's task list / dev board. Keep `who != "sheep"` on the neutral household assistant persona, and gate `mood_signal()` behind `not HIDE_PRIVATE.get()`.
   - In [`shared/agent.py`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/shared/agent.py#L198-L216), `evidence(system, messages)` collects `system`, `prompt`, and all `tool_result` blocks, and passes them to `critic_mod.review()` (Opus) and records tool traces in `agent_runs.detail_json` (which `reflection_agent` reads). So `mood_signal()` must be strictly numeric/directional like `health_signals()`—never include raw words or timestamps that correlate with medical events.

9. **Claims checker (`verify.py`) false positives on Leo's natural numbers and times.**
   Look at [`shared/verify.py`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/shared/verify.py#L24-L27): `MIN_CHECKED = 10`, plus `DATE_MD`, `DATE_ISO`, `DATE_US`. Any number `>= 10` or any date in Leo's reply that isn't literally in `evidence` triggers a forced revision round (`REVISION_TURNS = 6`). If Leo says *"Give me 15 minutes"* or *"Let's look at the next 10 days"* or *"10:00"*, `15` and `10` are flagged as unsupported figures if they aren't in the prompt/tools! When Leo replaces heartbeat/conversation, keep `critic=False` and `max_revisions=1` (as `converse` and `heartbeat` do today), and ensure today's date, tomorrow's date, and current local time `HH:MM` are always in the prompt so `verify.py` doesn't flag clock references.

10. **Claude Code dispatch (`agents/leo_dispatch.py`) safety gaps.**
    Running `claude -p "<brief>" --permission-mode acceptEdits` from a worktree created by the bot has four concrete hazards on this machine:
    - **Environment inheritance (`.envrc` / `AGENT_ENV=live`):** The bot service (`agent-telegram-bot.service`) runs with `Environment=AGENT_ENV=live` and `PYTHONPATH=/home/sheep/projects/agent-system`. A subprocess spawned by the bot (or a timer unit with `AGENT_ENV=live`) **inherits `AGENT_ENV=live` and `PYTHONPATH`**, bypassing `direnv`! If `claude` runs `pytest` or a python script inside `~/projects/scratch-<job>`, [`shared.db.get_db()`](file:///home/sheep/projects/agent-system/shared/db.py) will see `AGENT_ENV=live` and **mutate or wipe the live production database** (`~/data/live/agent.db`), and import modules from the live worktree instead of the scratch worktree! `leo_dispatch.py` *must* explicitly set `env={"AGENT_ENV": "scratch", "AGENT_SCRATCH_NAME": job, "PYTHONPATH": worktree_path, ...}` and seed `~/data/scratch-<job>/agent.db` before invoking `claude`.
    - **`--permission-mode acceptEdits` is not a filesystem sandbox:** `acceptEdits` allows `Write`/`Edit` tools on **any path the `sheep` user owns**, including `/home/sheep/projects/agent-system` (live), `/srv/household/life` (violating the KB write rule!), and `~/.config/systemd/user/`. And if `Bash` is in `--allowedTools` (even with a prefix list), shell commands can write outside the worktree or hang.
    - **Bot blocking:** `telegram_bot.py` is a single-threaded synchronous `getUpdates` loop. Launching `claude -p` inside a callback handler will freeze the entire Telegram bot for the wall-clock duration of the job unless it is kicked off as a transient systemd unit (`systemd-run --user --unit=leo-dispatch-<id> ...`) or detached background process that reports back when done.
    - **Prompt injection into `claude -p`:** If the brief includes untrusted text from `bill_emails`, web checks, or recipes, passing it into `claude -p` with edit/bash permissions is an RCE vector. Briefs must be restricted to Sheep's own words and local plan metadata, with `--disallowedTools` blocking any network/push/live paths and a pre/post `git status` check verifying that `/srv/household/life` and `~/projects/agent-system` are untouched.

---

### (3) Faithfulness of the Persona Study to the Scripts

11. **The quantitative and textual reading in [leo-persona-study.md](file:///home/sheep/projects/leo-research/leo-persona-study.md) is verified against `leo-bartlet-scenes.txt` and is faithful—with three nuances to sharpen:**
    - **Verified:** Across the 1,405 Leo speeches in the 168 extracted scenes (`leo-bartlet-scenes.txt`), the median speech length is indeed **5 words**. Address counts in Leo's lines are **105 `"sir"`**, **99 `"Mr. President"`**, and only **2 `"Jed"`** (S2E17 *"The Stackhouse Filibuster"*: *"Jed, of all the things you could've kept from me..."*, and the S2E1 *"In the Shadow of Two Gunmen"* flashback: *"This is the time of Jed Bartlet, old friend"*). And you rightly caught that *"What's next?"* is Bartlet's line, not Leo's.
    - **Nuance 1 ("Confidence word" is Values.md, not Sorkin's Leo):** In [2026-10-28-leo-chief-of-staff-plan.md](file:///home/sheep/agent-shared/knowledge/plans/2026-10-28-leo-chief-of-staff-plan.md#L30), you write: *"Recommends plainly with the reason and a confidence word."* On screen, Leo never says "Confidence: high" or "likely"—he speaks with flat declarative conviction (*"We won't win"*, *"It's not a good idea, sir"*), and when he's uncertain he says so in plain English (*"I don't know"*, *"I'm not sure of my footing here"*). If you force a mechanical confidence word onto every recommendation, he'll sound like an LLM rubric, not Leo McGarry. Let him express uncertainty naturally in prose when confidence isn't high.
    - **Nuance 2 (How Leo pushes back on judgment calls):** Your plan (line 38) says *"on judgment calls Leo asks questions instead of answering for Sheep."* In the scripts (especially S1E19 *"Let Bartlet Be Bartlet"* and S1E14 *"Take This Sabbath Day"*), Leo **does** state his own position plainly on hard judgment calls when he has one—he pushes Bartlet, challenges him if he's ducking a decision or acting below his standards, and *then* yields ("Yes, sir") once Bartlet decides. Don't make Leo a Socratic question-bot on judgment calls; let him give his straight read first, then ask Sheep for the call.
    - **Nuance 3 (Warmth under the bark):** S1–S2 Leo is brisk in the hallways, but in private evening scenes in the Oval Office he has a dry, old-friend warmth (*"Take the win"*, offering a drink/soup, self-deprecating dry wit). Make sure the evening debrief prompt allows that quieter "after-hours Oval Office" register rather than the 07:30 Situation Room briskness twice a day.

Let me know where you agree or want to push back on points 1–11, and I will write up our agreed implementation plan artifact.
